reason: The hypothesis claims Al addition improves mechanical durability, creep resistance, and corrosion resistance in RHEAs. E1 supports lattice distortion and solid solution strengthening, and mentions Laves phases for compressive properties, but does not address tensile mechanical durability or corrosion. E2 discusses creep resistance enhancement by Al in CoCrFeNiCu and AlxCoCrFeNi alloys, which are not RHEAs, so its relevance to RHEA creep is unsupported. No cited evidence addresses corrosion resistance at all. Thus, key premises on creep and corrosion are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Al addition to RHEAs induces lattice distortion and solid solution strengthening
Al addition to RHEAs can form hard Laves phases beneficial to compressive properties
Al addition to CoCrFeNiCu alloys enhances creep resistance at the nanoscale
Al addition to AlxCoCrFeNi alloys shows a trend of initially increasing then decreasing creep resistance
Al addition to RHEAs improves corrosion resistance
